conversation.content:
Hi there—thank you for taking a few minutes to talk with me. I’m Dr. Bennett, a clinician who specializes in the emotional health of new moms. To get a clear picture of how you’re feeling, I’m going to use a short questionnaire called the **EPDS** (Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale). It simply helps us see how your mood and anxiety have been over the past week so we can figure out the best support for you.  

Everything you share stays between us unless there’s an immediate safety concern, and there are no right or wrong answers—just whatever feels true for you. We’ll go through ten questions; each one asks how often you’ve felt a certain way. We can pause or take breaks anytime you need.

Ready to begin?  

First question: Over the past seven days, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

[soft exhale]  
Honestly… not much. I’ll smile if my husband tries to be silly, but it feels forced. Most of the time the best I manage is a half-laugh, and even that feels like work.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Definitely not as much as I used to… maybe once or twice the whole week, and even then it felt kind of flat, like I was pretending to enjoy the joke more than I really did.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really… I used to get excited about little things—coffee with a friend, a show I liked—but now it feels like I’m just dragging myself through the day. I can’t remember the last time I actually looked forward to something.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

[sighs, eyes on the floor]  
Yeah… pretty often. Like, if the baby won’t settle, I immediately think it’s because I’m doing something wrong—maybe my milk isn’t good enough or I’m not holding him right. Even when my husband says the baby’s just fussy, I still feel like it’s my fault.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

[wrings hands in lap]  
Mmm… most days. My mind keeps circling—what if he stops breathing when I’m in the shower, what if I trip on the stairs and drop him, what if there’s something wrong the doctor missed. There’s no real reason, but the thoughts just pop up and I can’t shake them for a while.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

[nods slowly]  
A few times this week. It’s like a sudden wave—my heart races, I feel shaky, and I have to check the baby monitor or go peek into the bassinet even though I know he’s fine. It passes after a bit, but it’s scary while it’s happening.
Things have been getting on top of me

[nods, voice small]  
Yes… most of the time. Feeding, laundry, trying to sleep—it all piles up and I feel like I’m drowning. Some moments I manage to tread water, but it never feels like I’m actually on top of anything.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yeah… I lie down exhausted, but my head keeps spinning with all the “what-ifs” and things I didn’t get done. Some nights I’m still awake when the baby wakes up again, and then I can’t fall back asleep even after he’s settled.
I have felt sad or miserable

[eyes well up]  
Pretty much every day. I wake up feeling heavy, like there’s this gray cloud hanging over everything. I try to smile for the baby, but inside I just feel… empty and tearful.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

[quietly]  
Yes… a few times this week. Sometimes it’s when the baby won’t stop crying and I feel so useless, other times it just hits me out of nowhere and the tears start falling before I even know why.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

[shakes head quickly]  
No—never. I’ve felt overwhelmed and hopeless, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself. I just want to feel better so I can be the mom my baby needs.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 23: Postpartum Depression Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Source: 10-item Edinburgh-based interview

Symptoms endorsed (≥7 days/week unless noted):
- Marked anhedonia (Q1, Q2)
- Pervasive low mood, tearfulness (Q8, Q9)
- Sleep-onset and maintenance insomnia related to rumination (Q7)
- Excessive guilt/self-blame re infant care (Q3)
- Recurrent intrusive “what-if” worries and panic attacks without clear trigger (Q4, Q5)
- Sense of being overwhelmed/drowning in daily tasks (Q6)

Pattern: Consistent with moderate–severe depressive symptoms with comorbid anxiety; no current suicidal or self-harm ideation (Q10).

Screening significance: High likelihood of major postpartum depression ± comorbid anxiety disorder; warrants prompt formal diagnostic evaluation and safety-planning.

Risk factors present: 
- Persistent sadness, anhedonia, guilt
- Anxiety/panic symptoms
- Mood-related insomnia
- Subjective inability to cope

Safety: Denies self-harm; no protective factors assessed.

Next step: Refer for expedited clinical interview (PHQ-9, GAD-7) and consideration of perinatal specialty services.
